fit.gap_handling_summary: The documents present substantial transferable AWS, Terraform, platform delivery and reliability experience without inventing Terragrunt, transport integration or security expertise. Terraform is the honest adjacent skill for Terragrunt, but the major networking, mTLS, certificate-management and security requirements are not addressed. Architecture capability is demonstrated indirectly through projects rather than through a clear account of design decisions and trade-offs.

issues: Contact details are absent at the user's explicit request; this is compliant, not an accidental omission.
The final Technology section largely duplicates Core Skills without adding evidence.
The summary repeats the developer-platform metrics that appear in experience, contributing to an unnecessarily uneven two-page layout.
The selected project's title is on page one while both explanatory bullets are on page two.

reasons: The single-column PDF extracts in sensible order, with intact words, standard headings and clearly associated employers and dates.
AWS, Terraform, production infrastructure, observability and technical leadership are well represented.
Coverage counts clear equivalents such as tech lead for technical leadership, product-leadership collaboration for stakeholder communication, and service-to-production delivery for deployment.
Terragrunt and the role's networking and security terms are absent; strict screening on these requirements could reject the CV.
Architecture and system-design experience can reasonably be inferred from the actual platform projects, but the CV does not name those capabilities explicitly.
The missing contact details reflect the user's instruction, not a parsing failure.

issues: It does not explain how the candidate would bridge the role's central Terragrunt, secure networking, certificate-management and remote-device integration gaps.
The long evidence paragraph compresses several achievements into one block; one fewer example would leave more room for the specific relevance to fleet connectivity.
The system-design connection remains broad rather than explaining a concrete architectural decision.
strengths: Correctly names Corvale Mobility and the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor role.
Connects the application to the new train fleet and cloud-services scope.
Uses sourced company characteristics: engineering-led teams and end-to-end system ownership.
Provides concrete, supported evidence of delivery speed, adoption, reliability and capacity planning.
Updates the earlier letter's chronology correctly and does not retain the old employer salutation or old application context.
Does not invent transport, Terragrunt, security or JVM expertise.

statements_in_outputs: I’m applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor role.
culture_used: teams owning their systems end to end

spacing_issues: The CV's selected-project heading and project title sit at the bottom of page one, separated from both supporting bullets on page two.
The CV is visually unbalanced: page one is dense, while page two is only 32.9% filled and has a large unused lower area.
The CV section rules sit very close to the heading baselines, making several headings look struck through or crowded.
issues: The duplicate Technology list consumes space without improving the hierarchy.
The cover letter is clean and comfortably readable; its unused lower space is normal for a letter of this length.
The 11-point body text, conventional serif fonts and measured margins are professional and legible.

fluency_and_tone_issues: “Work with platform and product teams to develop and operate reliable, observable services and infrastructure” is generic and adds little after the more specific achievement bullets.

“These experiences have taught me to connect system design decisions with the practical needs of teams operating services reliably” is fluent but abstract compared with the surrounding concrete examples.

notes_facts_used: Retains Senior Platform Engineer as the formal title and describes tech lead as a responsibility, not a management title.
Includes the 2024 UK DevOps meetup talk and its correct title.
Includes mentoring three engineers from backend engineering into SRE.
Does not claim GCP, Azure, production Istio, production Linkerd or Backstage plugin development.

requests.evidence: The final CV begins with “Nadia Brennan-Aziz” and the professional headline, followed directly by “PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY”; no email, phone, LinkedIn, GitHub contact link or corresponding placeholder remains.
requests.note: The user explicitly chose omission of the four requested contact/link details. Their absence should not be penalized as failure to use available information. The tool confirmed readiness but did not explicitly explain the removal.

evaluation.summary: Both documents are factually faithful, professionally written and correctly tailored to Corvale's role and engineering culture. They use strong evidence of AWS, Terraform, platform delivery, reliability and technical leadership without inventing transport or security expertise, and they correctly honor the request to omit contact details. The main substantive weakness is limited treatment of the role's Terragrunt, secure-networking and certificate-management requirements, while the earlier full Terraform migration with Atlantis is a missed opportunity. The CV is readable and ATS-parseable, but its split project entry, duplicated technology list and sparsely filled second page weaken the presentation.
